root_cause.text: The fbdev deferred-I/O implementation stored VMA fault/writeback state inside `struct fb_info`/`struct fb_deferred_io`, so a hot-unplug could free that object while userspace still had an active framebuffer mapping, leaving `fb_deferred_io_fault()` and `fb_deferred_io_track_page()` to dereference freed/undefined state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly says “Disconnect deferred I/O from the lifetime of struct fb_info” and fixes the case where “device hot-unplug happens while user space still has an active mapping”; in the diff, `vm_private_data` is changed from `info` to a new `fb_deferred_io_state`, and `fb_deferred_io_cleanup()` now sets `fbdefio_state->info = NULL` so later faults return `VM_FAULT_SIGBUS` instead of accessing the freed `fb_info`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Introduce reference-counted deferred framebuffer IO state management to preserve VMA lifetime safety.
intent_record.what: Added a new reference-counted `struct fb_deferred_io_state` with a mutex and helper functions for allocation, get/put, and release; added `vm_open` and `vm_close` callbacks that acquire and release a reference via `vma->vm_private_data`.
intent_record.how: This makes the deferred framebuffer I/O state lifetime explicitly tied to VMA references, so the backing state is kept alive while mappings exist and is destroyed only after the last close, preventing use-after-free or premature cleanup of shared deferred-IO data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Serialize deferred framebuffer fault handling and add a device-gone check to prevent races and invalid page faults.
intent_record.what: The function fb_deferred_io_fault() was changed to use a fb_deferred_io_state pointer from vmf->vma->vm_private_data instead of directly treating vm_private_data as struct fb_info. It now acquires fbdefio_state->lock at entry, reads info from fbdefio_state->info, checks whether info is NULL, and routes all SIGBUS error returns through a common err_mutex_unlock path that releases the mutex before returning. The successful path also explicitly unlocks the mutex before assigning vmf->page and returning 0.
intent_record.how: This makes the page-fault handler synchronized against concurrent state changes and safe against the framebuffer device being removed while a fault is in progress. If the device is gone or the offset is invalid or no page can be retrieved, the handler now fails cleanly with VM_FAULT_SIGBUS after releasing the lock, preventing use-after-free or races on stale info state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Make deferred framebuffer page tracking safely fail with SIGBUS when the device has been removed, preventing invalid access to freed or missing framebuffer state.
intent_record.what: The function `fb_deferred_io_track_page()` was changed to take a `struct fb_deferred_io_state *fbdefio_state` instead of `struct fb_info *info`. Inside the function, `info` and `fbdefio` are now declared separately, `mutex_lock()` uses `fbdefio_state->lock` instead of `fbdefio->lock`, and the code now assigns `info = fbdefio_state->info` and checks `if (!info)` to return `VM_FAULT_SIGBUS` via `err_mutex_unlock` before dereferencing `info->fbdefio`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the page-tracking path now tolerates the framebuffer device being gone by detecting a missing `info` pointer and failing the fault with `SIGBUS` instead of dereferencing a stale or NULL device pointer. The locking is also tied to the deferred-IO state object, which keeps synchronization available even when the framebuffer info has already been detached.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix deferred framebuffer page-mkwrite handling to use the correct deferred-IO state and add VMA open/close lifecycle hooks.
intent_record.what: The page-mkwrite path was changed to take a `struct fb_deferred_io_state *` instead of `struct fb_info *`, and the call chain was updated so `fb_deferred_io_mkwrite()` reads `vm_private_data` as `fb_deferred_io_state` and passes that into `fb_deferred_io_page_mkwrite()`. In the tracking function, mutex unlocks were switched from `fbdefio->lock` to `fbdefio_state->lock`. The `fb_deferred_io_vm_ops` table also gained `.open = fb_deferred_io_vm_open` and `.close = fb_deferred_io_vm_close` entries.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the deferred framebuffer write-fault handling now operates on the deferred-IO state object rather than the framebuffer info object, which aligns the page tracking and locking with the per-VMA deferred-IO context. Adding open/close VM ops means the mapping now participates in VMA lifecycle management, likely allowing deferred-IO state to be initialized and released correctly when the mapping is opened or torn down.

intent_record.intent_summary: Make framebuffer deferred I/O mmap hold a reference to the deferred I/O state instead of fb_info so the mapping uses the correct lifetime-managed private data.
intent_record.what: In fb_deferred_io_mmap(), the assignment to vma->vm_private_data was changed from info to info->fbdefio_state, and a new fb_deferred_io_state_get(info->fbdefio_state) call was added with a comment noting it will be released in vma->vm_ops->close().
intent_record.how: The VMA now stores the deferred I/O state object rather than the fb_info pointer, and the added reference acquisition keeps that state alive for the lifetime of the mmap mapping until the VMA close path drops it.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the deferred I/O state lock in fb_deferred_io_work() instead of the fbdefio lock to synchronize the correct object.
intent_record.what: The function `fb_deferred_io_work()` adds a new local pointer `fbdefio_state` initialized from `info->fbdefio_state`, and changes the mutex acquisition from `fbdefio->lock` to `fbdefio_state->lock`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, deferred framebuffer I/O work now serializes using the lock stored in the framebuffer deferred I/O state object instead of the lock in `fbdefio`, which changes the synchronization target for this work path and likely ensures it operates on the correct state instance.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix deferred framebuffer I/O to use the correct state lock when releasing the mutex.
intent_record.what: The unlock in fb_deferred_io_work() was changed from mutex_unlock(&fbdefio->lock) to mutex_unlock(&fbdefio_state->lock), and fb_deferred_io_init() gained a new local declaration for struct fb_deferred_io_state *fbdefio_state.
intent_record.how: Runtime locking now targets the fb_deferred_io_state object rather than the fb_deferred_io object, which fixes use of the correct mutex instance and prevents mismatched lock/unlock behavior or corruption of deferred I/O state synchronization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allocate and initialize deferred framebuffer IO state during setup, with proper ENOMEM handling when allocation fails.
intent_record.what: In fb_deferred_io_init(), the code replacing mutex_init(&fbdefio->lock) now allocates a deferred-IO state object with fb_deferred_io_state_alloc(), returns -ENOMEM if allocation fails, and stores the current fb_info pointer in fbdefio_state->info before continuing initialization.
intent_record.how: This changes deferred framebuffer IO setup to depend on dynamically allocated state rather than only initializing a mutex, and it introduces an out-of-memory failure path if the state cannot be created. It also records the associated fb_info in the new state so later deferred IO handling can access the framebuffer instance through that state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Store the deferred I/O state in fb_info and use the proper release helper during init failure cleanup.
intent_record.what: In fb_deferred_io_init(), the code now assigns info->fbdefio_state = fbdefio_state before returning success, and on the error path it replaces mutex_destroy(&fbdefio->lock) with fb_deferred_io_state_release(fbdefio_state).
intent_record.how: This makes the deferred I/O state object reachable from the fb_info structure when initialization succeeds, and ensures cleanup on failure is performed through the dedicated state-release helper rather than destroying only the mutex directly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix fb deferred I/O cleanup to detach, clear, and release fb_deferred_io_state safely instead of directly destroying the old lock.
intent_record.what: In fb_deferred_io_cleanup(), a new local pointer fbdefio_state is introduced from info->fbdefio_state. After fb_deferred_io_lastclose(info), the code now sets info->fbdefio_state to NULL, takes fbdefio_state->lock, clears fbdefio_state->info, unlocks it, and drops a reference with fb_deferred_io_state_put(fbdefio_state). The call to mutex_destroy(&fbdefio->lock) is removed, while kvfree(info->pagerefs) and fbdefio->mapping = NULL remain.
intent_record.how: This changes cleanup to properly detach and release the deferred I/O state object associated with the framebuffer info, preventing stale back-references and ensuring the state object is reference-counted out of existence safely. It also avoids destroying the old mutex directly here, implying lock lifetime is now managed by the state object's teardown path instead of this cleanup function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the embedded mutex from `fb_deferred_io` and forward-declare a new deferred-IO state type to support an internal structure change.
intent_record.what: In `struct fb_deferred_io`, the `struct mutex lock` field and its comment were removed, and a forward declaration `struct fb_deferred_io_state;` was added before the `#endif`.
intent_record.how: This changes the public structure layout by eliminating an embedded mutex from `fb_deferred_io`, while introducing an opaque type name that can be referenced elsewhere without exposing its definition here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add deferred I/O state storage to `fb_info` for later use by framebuffer deferred I/O handling.
intent_record.what: A new field, `struct fb_deferred_io_state *fbdefio_state;`, was added to `struct fb_info` immediately after `fbdefio` within the `#ifdef`-guarded deferred I/O section.
intent_record.how: This extends the framebuffer info structure to carry an additional deferred I/O state pointer, allowing code using `fb_info` to track or access per-device deferred I/O state at runtime.

consistency_review.core_intent: Harden framebuffer deferred I/O by consistently using and reference-managing fb_deferred_io_state for locking, mmap, page-mkwrite, and cleanup lifecycle safety.
Serialize deferred framebuffer fault handling and add device-gone handling so page faults fail safely with SIGBUS after device removal.
Allocate, initialize, store, and correctly release deferred framebuffer I/O state during framebuffer setup and failure cleanup.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause: deferred-I/O state was previously stored in fb_info/fb_deferred_io and could be freed while mappings were still active. This patch group introduces reference-counted fb_deferred_io_state, updates mmap/page-mkwrite and VMA lifecycle handling, and ensures cleanup detaches and releases the state safely, preventing use-after-free of deferred-I/O state after hot-unplug.

The changes directly address the root cause by adding device-gone handling and safe failure paths for deferred framebuffer faults/page tracking after hot-unplug, preventing use of freed fb_info/fb_deferred_io state.

The changes manage allocation, storage, and cleanup of deferred fbdev I/O state in fb_info, which is directly tied to the root cause where that state could be freed while mappings still used it. Properly handling lifetime and release of the deferred-I/O object addresses the vulnerability class.

This change is only an internal deferred-IO structure refactor (removing an embedded mutex and forward-declaring a new state type). It does not directly address the use-after-free caused by fb_info/fb_deferred_io state being freed while mappings remain active, nor does it add lifetime management or fault/writeback safety for hot-unplug.

The change adds deferred-I/O state storage to fb_info, which is directly part of the vulnerable design where deferred-I/O state lived in fb_info/fb_deferred_io and could be freed on hot-unplug while mappings still existed.

candidates.rationale: This stores a raw fb_info pointer in the VMA private data, so the mapping keeps referencing fb_info after hot-unplug even though the deferred-I/O state may already be freed, leading to use-after-free in fault/writeback paths.
The fault handler dereferences VMA private data that was set to fb_info, so if the device has been removed and that object is freed, the fault path can access invalid state.
This directly pulls deferred-I/O state from fb_info without any lifetime protection; if hot-unplug has freed or invalidated fb_info/fbdefio, page tracking will dereference stale memory.
The deferred work path also relies on fb_info holding the deferred-I/O state, so the same lifetime bug can surface when the workqueue races with device removal.
Destroying the lock embedded in the deferred-I/O object without first detaching/invalidating active mappings contributes to the lifetime hazard by allowing later VMA callbacks to use freed state.

vuln_statements.explanation: This stores fb_info directly in the VMA private data, so later fault/writeback callbacks keep using fb_info after hot-unplug may have freed the deferred-I/O state, creating the use-after-free root cause.
The fault handler retrieves fb_info from VMA private data and then uses it without lifetime protection; if the framebuffer device was removed, this dereference can access freed state.
This directly dereferences deferred-I/O state through fb_info, so after hot-unplug the fbdefio pointer may be stale or freed, leading to invalid memory access in page tracking and work paths.
Destroying the lock inside the deferred-I/O object without first detaching or invalidating active mappings leaves VMA callbacks able to race with freed state.
